question: Which side of the road should you normally drive on in the UK?
explain: Rule 160: You should keep to the left unless overtaking or turning right.

question: When may you move onto the right-hand side of a two-way road?
options: When overtaking or passing a parked vehicle safely
explain: Rule 160: You only move right when overtaking. Passing an obstruction, or turning right, and when it is safe.

question: What should you do after you finish overtaking on a two-way road?
options: Move back to the left as soon as it is safe
explain: Rule 160: Return to the left side smoothly once you are safely past.

question: Which lane should you use on a multi-lane dual carriageway when you are not overtaking?
explain: Rule 160: Highway Code Rule 264 says keep in the left lane unless overtaking.

question: After turning left or right into a side road, where should your car end up?
options: In the middle of the road
On the left side of that road
explain: Rule 160: Always finish your turn on the left side of the new road.

question: Why should you not hug the centre line on a bend?
options: An oncoming vehicle could hit you
It is illegal to steer left
explain: Rule 160: Keeping left gives oncoming traffic room. Especially where you cannot see round a bend.

question: If you pass a row of parked cars on your left. What should you do afterwards?
options: Return to the left when there is room
explain: Rule 160: Move back to the left once past the parked cars. So oncoming traffic has space.

question: What does keeping left help prevent on narrow residential streets?
explain: Rule 160: Staying on your side leaves a clear path for oncoming drivers and cyclists.
